title: Executable intent monitoring and argument integrity harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Recent model and routing config changes have produced subtle regressions in function selection and malformed argument generation for downstream tools. We need a lightweight, automated harness that continuously evaluates 'executable intent' — whether the model chooses the correct tool and whether the produced args match the tool contract. Goal: produce a reproducible pipeline that runs in shadow mode against live traffic and model rollout candidates, emits granular metrics (selection accuracy, arg-schema-violation rate, confidence drift), raises alerts on configurable deltas, and integrates with the Console rollouts dashboard and our regression alerting playbook. Scope: selection accuracy, argument validation (type/shape/range), end-to-end example traces, and compact daily reports. Not in scope: full automatic remediation or rewrites of prompts (separate feature).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Harness runs nightly against a canonical baseline dataset (>= 5k multi-turn cases) and a shadow sample of live requests (configurable sample rate).

A2: Tool-selection accuracy is computed per-model and per-config and baseline vs candidate deltas are tracked; alert fires when selection accuracy drops by >1.5 percentage points or relative drop >5%.
A3: Argument validation checks run against the registered tool schema; failures are categorized (missing fields, type mismatch, constraint violation) and aggregated by tool and model version.
A4: Each failing example includes model response, parsed args, matched schema, and a suggested minimal repro prompt; outputs are linked to a GitHub issue or Confluence eval artifact.
A5: Results are exported to Console as a per-route dashboard and time-series for 90 days; alerts surface in PagerDuty / Slack with links to example traces.
implementation_steps: Step 1: Assemble canonical eval set from existing tool-invocation logs and curated positives/negatives (owner: Marco).
Step 2: Implement parser that normalizes model outputs into canonical call records and maps to tool registry (owner: Priya).
Step 3: Reuse existing schema registry to validate args; add lightweight validators for ranges and common coercions (owner: Lin).
Step 4: Shadow runner: integrate harness into inference routing layer to mirror a sampled subset of live requests to the harness without affecting responses (owner: infra team).
Step 5: Metricization: implement selection_accuracy, arg_failure_rate, confidence_delta, and latency overhead monitoring; emit Prometheus metrics and Console events (owner: telemetry).
Step 6: Alerting: add alert rules and automated weekly regression summaries emailed to SRE/ML/PM teams (owner: oncall).
Step 7: QA: run against historical config/model rollback window to validate signal and calibrate thresholds (owner: QA).
Step 8: Docs & Playbook: write triage guide, recommended remediation steps, and integration knobs for Dedicated/Private customers (owner: Docs).
updates: 2026-02-18 - Aisha: Ticket created after spike where a model rollout increased arg-missing errors for payment tools. Initial scope proposed.
2026-02-25 - Marco: Collected 6.2k candidate examples from last 30 days across /chat and /generate routes. Stored anonymized payloads in s3://redwood-evals/executable-intent/2026-02.

2026-03-03 - Lin: Prototype validator implemented that catches 3 classes of arg failures. Fast path uses JSON schema, fallback includes heuristic coercion for numeric strings. Early results: 0.8% arg-failure baseline on curated set.

2026-03-06 - Priya: Parser edge cases found for function-calling formatted as prose rather than JSON; added a recovered-JSON heuristic to avoid false negatives (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/intent-parser).

2026-03-10 - Marco: Shadow runner proof-of-concept deployed to canary cluster with 0.5% sample of live traffic; observed selection accuracy delta between baseline-model:v1 and candidate-model:v2 = -2.1 percentage points on sample (investigating whether prompt truncation changed behavior).

2026-03-12 - Review: SRE flagged potential 12ms median extra latency for sampled requests in the canary path; decided to move heavy validation to async post-run path and keep only selection signal in fast path.

2026-03-13 - Decision: Thresholds set to absolute drop >1.5pp or relative drop >5% for selection accuracy; arg-failure alert threshold set to 0.5% absolute increase. Added dependency on ENG-47102 (toolcall-canary-harness) for rollout integration.
release_notes: Introduces an executable-intent eval harness that detects regressions in tool selection and argument generation during model/config rollouts.
Provides Console dashboards and alerting rules to notify teams on selection-accuracy and arg-validation regressions.
Adds a lightweight shadow runner with async validators to avoid production latency impact.
